question: Can very deep ResNets be trained faster and with lower test error by randomly skipping residual blocks during training while keeping full depth at test time?
hypothesis: Shortening the expected depth during training strengthens gradients in early layers and acts as an implicit ensemble/regulariser, improving error and speed.
contributions: Stochastic depth: randomly drop whole ResBlocks per mini-batch with linearly decaying survival probability
Lower test error on CIFAR-10/100 and SVHN, and a 1202-layer ResNet at 4.91% on CIFAR-10

method.summary: Each residual block l is multiplied by a Bernoulli b_l with survival probability p_l = 1 - (l/L)(1-p_L), dropping it to identity for the mini-batch. At test time all blocks are active and f_l output is scaled by p_l. Compared against constant-depth ResNets (He et al.) with identical optimiser settings.

datasets.name: CIFAR-100
datasets.split: same as CIFAR-10 (inferred from 'same train-test split')
datasets.preprocessing: same augmentation as CIFAR-10; also run without augmentation

datasets.name: SVHN
datasets.split: validation 6,000: 400 per class from train plus 200 per class from additional
datasets.preprocessing: mean subtraction, divide by std; no augmentation; all training samples used

models.name: ResNet-152 (ImageNet)
models.architecture: 50 bottleneck blocks, learned linear projection on mismatched shortcuts

training.lr_schedule: CIFAR: divide by 10 after epochs 250 and 375; 1202-layer: 0.01 for first 10 epochs then 0.1, divide by 10 at 150 and 225; SVHN: divide by 10 after epochs 30 and 35; ImageNet: fb.resnet.torch settings, lr 1e-4 after epoch 90 for the 120-epoch run
training.epochs: CIFAR 500; 1202-layer 300; SVHN 50; ImageNet 90 (baseline, also 120 for both)
training.regularisation: stochastic depth itself, p_L=0.5 linear decay
training.wall_clock: Table 2: CIFAR10+ 20h 42m vs 15h 7m; CIFAR100+ 20h 51m vs 15h 20m; SVHN 33h 43m vs 25h 33m (constant vs stochastic)

other.reporting: test error from the epoch with lowest validation error
other.svhn_depth_selection: depth and lr schedule chosen by optimising baseline validation error
other.weight_decay_other_datasets: SVHN and ImageNet weight decay not stated beyond 'same as' fb.resnet.torch

inference.samples: single run per configuration (inferred: no repeats mentioned)

metrics.name: test error
metrics.definition: top-1 classification error at epoch of lowest validation error

eval.protocol: Single training runs; no seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests reported.

results.quote:
ResNets trained with stochastic depth
yield a further relative improvement of 18% and result in 5.25% test error.

results.quote: to a 4.91% test error without sign of overﬁtting

results.claim: The constant-depth 1202-layer ResNet is worse than the 110-layer one (6.67% vs 6.41%).
results.quote:
yields a test error of

terms.definition: randomly dropping entire ResBlocks per mini-batch, bypassing them with identity, and keeping full depth at test time
p_l = Pr(b_l = 1), the probability ResBlock l is active

lineage.work: Deep residual learning for image recognition (He et al.)

lineage.note: analogy; makes network shorter not thinner

code.snippet: H_l = ReLU(b_l f_l(H_{l-1}) + id(H_{l-1})); p_l = 1 - (l/L)(1 - p_L); test: H_l = ReLU(p_l f_l(H_{l-1}) + H_{l-1})
